name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies using Pret. This keeps our codebase clean without risking logic changes, since Pret only touches formatting. The trade-off is trusting Pret’s safety checks—we accept the risk of missed edge cases to avoid manual whitespace cleanup.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just upstream noise—it’s that auto-applying even whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies creates a false sense of cleanliness while masking deeper issues. A better alternative is to fork the dependency, apply formatting changes manually, and submit a PR upstream; this forces review of the actual changes and avoids hidden drift. Settle it by running a diff between the auto-applied result and the manual PR to confirm no unintended whitespace or metadata leaks.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk is that auto-applying whitespace patches to third-party code introduces hidden drift—future updates to those dependencies may fail silently if Pret’s formatting doesn’t match upstream, or worse, mask actual bugs by normalizing inconsistent style. A better alternative is to enforce formatting at *our* boundaries: run Pret only on our code, and document a clear policy for contributors to format their own changes before merging. Settle it by running a controlled experiment: apply Pret to a single dependency, then update it twice—once with Pret’s changes, once without—and measure CI failures or merge conflicts.
